messages.subject: Ordering character vector variables by default, or no?
parts:
This came up in a discussion surrounding a question over at SO. On my
machine this code:

dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()

results in a plot with the x axis ticks labeled in reverse
alphabetical order, as the values appear in the data frame. (I've
coerced x to character here; normally I run R with
stringsAsFactors=FALSE) Others seemed to see different behavior,
namely that ggplot would sort the data frame first, so the resulting
plot would have the x axis labels in alphabetical order.

Any ideas what could be causing this?

parts: Hi:

On Mon, Jul 18, 2011 at 2:19 PM, Joran <joran...@gmail.com> wrote:
> This came up in a discussion surrounding a question over at SO. On my
> machine this code:
>
> dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
> ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()

I get it in alphabetical order. Even if printed as a factor, it should
still plot in alphabetical order because of the ordering of the factor
levels (default is lexical ordering).
str(dat1)
'data.frame': 5 obs. of 2 variables:
$ x: Factor w/ 5 levels "a","b","c","d",..: 5 4 3 2 1
$ y: num 0.568 0.215 0.509 0.756 0.739

To 'guarantee' reversed alphabetical order, define x as an ordered factor:

dat2 <- data.frame(x = factor(letters[5:1], levels = letters[5:1]),
y = runif(5))
> str(dat2)
'data.frame': 5 obs. of 2 variables:
$ x: Factor w/ 5 levels "e","d","c","b",..: 1 2 3 4 5
$ y: num 0.993 0.21 0.651 0.729 0.486

# reversed alphabetical order (conforms to level ordering)
ggplot(dat2, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
# alphabetical order (x is now character rather than ordered factor)
ggplot(dat2, aes(x = as.character(x), y)) + geom_point()

HTH,
Dennis

> I get it in alphabetical order.

I do not, and my question is why.

I understand perfectly well how to ensure a particular ordering using
ordered factors. My question related to the fact that when I store
that variable as a _character_ I do not appear to be seeing the same
behavior (i.e. default lexical ordering) that other people are seeing.
Instead, on my machine ggplot appears to be plotting them in the order
they happen to appear in the data frame. That's why I provided my
sessionInfo().

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Ordering character vector variables by default, or no?
parts:
On 7/18/2011 2:19 PM, Joran wrote:
> This came up in a discussion surrounding a question over at SO. On my
> machine this code:
>
> dat1<- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
> ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()
>
> results in a plot with the x axis ticks labeled in reverse
> alphabetical order, as the values appear in the data frame. (I've
> coerced x to character here; normally I run R with
> stringsAsFactors=FALSE) Others seemed to see different behavior,
> namely that ggplot would sort the data frame first, so the resulting
> plot would have the x axis labels in alphabetical order.
>
> Any ideas what could be causing this?

It has to do with your setting of stringsAsFactors to FALSE. I can
create both behaviors:

(sAF <- getOption("stringsAsFactors"))

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()
options(stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()

options(stringsAsFactors = sAF)


The former has the axis ordered e -> a, the latter a -> e. My guess is
that somewhere in the code, each relevant part of dat1 is being coerced
into a dataframe (I've seen something like this) and the different
stringsAsFactors options have a different effect. When TRUE, the axis
is ordered by the fact it is turned into a factor; when FALSE, it
maintains the ordering in the data.frame.

I'll leave it as a discussion point as to whether ggplot should behave
differently with different values of the stringsAsFactors options. On
one hand, changing a default option means you want a different behavior
than the default, so things may not work as per default/documented. On
the other hand, this is probably not an intended consequence of changing
the default and the principle of least astonishment would say to not
change behavior because of it.

On Jul 19, 8:46 am, Brian Diggs <dig...@ohsu.edu> wrote:
> It has to do with your setting of stringsAsFactors to FALSE.  I can

> options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
> dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
> ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()
>

> dat1 <- data.frame(x=letters[5:1],y=runif(5))
> ggplot(dat1,aes(x=as.character(x),y=y)) + geom_point()
>
> options(stringsAsFactors = sAF)
Ah, thanks, that makes sense!

> I'll leave it as a discussion point as to whether ggplot should behave
> differently with different values of the stringsAsFactors options.  On
> one hand, changing a default option means you want a different behavior
> than the default, so things may not work as per default/documented.  On
> the other hand, this is probably not an intended consequence of changing
> the default and the principle of least astonishment would say to not
> change behavior because of it.

If it were me I guess I would opt for ggplot to enforce lexical
ordering even when stringsAsFactors is set to FALSE. If you want a
specific, non-'standard' ordering, that's what ordered factors are
there for. But that's just my two cents.
